generatePrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: architectural room illustration for slide 7 of the existing SimuNow product pitch deck. One raster illustration only, without slide text or UI.
Primary request: a clear cutaway axonometric concept of a small office showing a wall air conditioner, four occupied-seat locations, an intentionally simplified straight supply-direction preview and furniture obstruction. This communicates local geometric rules, not CFD or a thermal field.
Scene/backdrop: white studio background, small rectangular office with light-gray floor, two pale walls, one large window, four light desks with monitors and charcoal office chairs, and one freestanding tall gray storage cabinet or divider between the air conditioner and a rear desk.
Subject: one white split air conditioner high on the left rear wall. A small number of thin translucent teal straight rays form an angular geometric fan in the chosen supply direction. The rays physically stop at the front surface of the tall furniture obstacle; no rays go through solid furniture or continue behind it. Other clear rays end finitely inside the room. No curves, vortices, particles, or streamlines.
Style/medium: refined architectural 3D illustration, matte materials, restrained detail, consistent with the existing SimuNow white-gray-teal office concepts. Natural geometry and soft contact shadows.
Composition/framing: landscape about 4:3, elevated three-quarter cutaway, whole room visible, furnishings clearly distinguishable, room centered with modest white margins. Four small teal circular markers are placed at the occupied-seat locations, each readable as a concept marker, not data.
Color palette: white, cool light gray, charcoal, teal #277F89 and pale cyan #57BCC7. Do not add thermal heatmap colors.
Text: no text, labels, numerals, logos or watermark. Editable explanatory text and captions will be placed in PowerPoint separately.
Constraints: a single office and one air conditioner; realistic architectural scale; abstract geometric preview only; no actual result values, temperatures, air speeds, comfort scores, savings numbers, dashboard, interface frame, or fake software screenshot. No geometry dimensions. Keep the image visually quiet for a professional academic product presentation.
edits:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Edit target: the generated office concept.
Change only the teal airflow graphic. Keep the entire office, air conditioner, furniture, people, four seat markers, camera, lighting and white background unchanged.
Remove all broad translucent teal sheets/fans. Instead show exactly five thin straight teal geometric line segments, starting at the air-conditioner outlet and fanning slightly downward into the room. Each is a single straight finite segment, not a curved streamline. The two rays aimed at the tall cabinet must visibly end at its front or top surface, with no continuation through or behind the cabinet. The three other rays must end at clear interior points before reaching any wall or window. No ray may protrude outside the room. No shaded cone or area fill. No added arrows, text, result values, or new objects.
This is an abstract geometric supply-direction/obstruction concept for a product slide, not CFD or physical data.

Change only the thin cyan rays. Preserve every other pixel as closely as possible, including room, desks, air conditioner, cabinet, people and four seat markers.
Remove ALL current cyan rays. Draw only THREE short, thin, straight cyan line segments from the air-conditioner outlet to the LEFT/TOP visible surface of the tall gray cabinet. ALL THREE segments must terminate visibly on the cabinet, with tiny endpoint dots. There must be NO cyan rays anywhere to the right of the cabinet, behind the cabinet, on the window, above the desks, or extending toward the far wall. The cabinet blocks all three rays. No cones, shaded sheets, curved paths, new text, arrows, or other graphics. This is a simple illustrative obstruction concept, not simulated airflow.
disclosure: Illustrative geometry and obstruction. Not an application screenshot, physical flow field, measured room or comfort result.
